items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Donald Voorhees was the conductor... he recommended me to take his place with “The Bell Telephone Hour”

ctx.x: So you worked on the technique of the bass with him. And your jazz playing, was that something you worked on with him or was that more self-taught?

Well I did jazz playing, not so much with him, no. He had a feel for it. You know he was with the Philharmonic and he taught at Juilliard during that period. He wasn’t a jazz player but he was loose. He was a good golfer, he was a marvelous painter, and he loved the bass, he adored the bass. And he was just — I studied privately and he taught at Juilliard but I just studied privately with him. And as time went on he was very kind to me and I used to come in evenings and he’d play duets with me and things like…
Symphony and as well as the dance orchestra. Eddie Safranski and I were the two hot guys, and they would add us to the other six who were playing with the NBC Orchestra.
